**PTZ Camera Selection and Road Coverage Analysis**

# **1\. Introduction**

This document evaluates camera options for night-time road surveillance across the street network and the Lotus building section. The requirement is human and vehicle detection at night; facial identification is not required.

**Why PTZ over bullet cameras.** Bullet cameras need a site visit and labour each time their view is adjusted. PTZ cameras can be re-aimed, zoomed and re-preset from a phone. Some models also support auto-tracking, which can be enabled later without new hardware.. The limitation of a PTZ is that it covers one direction at a time. In critical areas, cheaper supplementary cameras can fill the gaps once they are identified on site. Cameras are kept on fixed presets rather than auto-patrol, which would create blind periods.

**Layout Assumptions.** Cameras are mounted on street-light poles spaced about 30 m apart, at up to 10 m height. Road lengths are approximate upper values taken from Google Maps.

**Site inspection.** Before installation, each road must be checked on the ground for tree canopy or other obstructions blocking the camera view, and for critical spots that need supplementary cameras. Road lengths should also be confirmed at the same time.

# **4\. Street-Based Camera Designs**

## **4.1 200 m Roads \[3 streets\]**

### **Option A — Single camera, minimum infrastructure**

**1 × DS-2DE7A425IW-AEB(T5) — 200 m IR — RM3,102**

**![][image4]**

This uses the camera near its full rated IR distance. Street lighting at the far end improves reliability. The camera covers the entire road length but cannot observe both ends simultaneously.

| Item | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Cameras** | 1 |
| **Night IR** | 200 m |
| **Human/vehicle classification** | Yes |
| **Simultaneous both-direction coverage** | No |
| **Camera cost** | RM3,102 |
| **Power supply required** | Hi-PoE or 24VAC |

###  

### **Option B — Two cameras, better security**

**2 × DS-2DE5425 — 150 m IR — RM3,318**

Place one camera at each end, each covering its half of the road.

![][image5]

Each unit handles approximately 100 m of its assigned half, with 150 m of rated IR — providing a 50 m margin for overlap and low-light tolerance. Both ends are monitored simultaneously.

The camera-only price difference between Option A and Option B is RM216. The practical difference is the cost of a second installation point.

Budget variant: 1× 150 m \+ 1× 50 m Dahua \= **RM2,373**. Acceptable only where street lighting at the Dahua end is reliable.

 

 

## **4.2 300 m Roads \[ 2 streets\]**

**2 × DS-2DE5425 — 150 m IR — RM3,318**

**![][image6]**

This configuration matches the camera's rated range almost exactly. One camera at each end, each assigned 150 m. No other combination offers comparable performance at lower cost for this road length.

Alternatives considered: three 100 m cameras at RM4,563, one 200 m plus one 100 m at RM4,623, and one 250 m plus one 50 m at over RM6,000. None justifies the additional cost or complexity for this road length. For sections identified as higher priority during site inspection, a short- to medium-range supplementary camera — such as the Dahua SD29404DB-GNY at RM714 — can be added at a specific point of concern without reworking the primary two-camera layout. This is best determined after the site visit rather than planned upfront.

 

## **4.3 350 m Roads \[ 3 streets \]**

### **Option A — Two cameras, infrastructure-efficient**

**1 × DS-2DE7A425 \+ 1 × DS-2DE5425 — RM4,761**

**![][image7]**

One camera takes the longer section at approximately 200 m; the second handles the remaining 150 m. Two installation points required.

### **Option B — Three cameras, security-first**

**3 × DS-2DE5425 — 150 m IR — RM4,977**

Total rated IR coverage of 450 m across a 350 m road provides approximately 100 m of combined margin for overlap and dark-area tolerance.

![][image8]The camera cost difference between the two options is RM216. Option B requires one additional pole. For roads where lighting conditions are uncertain or security priority is high, three cameras is the stronger design.

An intermediate option — 2× 150 m \+ 1× 50 m Dahua \= RM4,032 — is viable if an additional camera location can be installed for under RM729, though it carries no spare IR margin. In this arrangement the three cameras together reach exactly 350 m, so the 50 m unit is required for full coverage rather than being an optional addition, and there is no spare IR margin at any boundary. The higher-risk section should therefore fall within the 150–200 m band, or the positions should be shifted so that it does. Final placement should be confirmed during site inspection once specific risk points are known.

 

## **4.4 400 m Roads — 2 streets**

### **Option A — Three cameras — Recommended**

**3 × DS-2DE5425 — 150 m IR — RM4,977**

450 m of aggregate rated IR across a 400 m road leaves approximately 50 m of margin.

![][image9]

### **Option B — Two cameras, fewer installations**

**2 × DS-2DE7A425IW-AEB(T5) — 200 m IR — RM6,204**

**![][image10]**

Two installation points instead of three, but RM1,227 more in camera cost and requiring Hi-PoE supply at both locations.

 

## **4.5 450 m Roads  \[1 street\]**

### **Option A — 3 × DS-2DE5425 — 150 m IR — RM4,977**

**![][image11]**Three cameras cover the 450 m road exactly, each assigned its rated distance. No alternative configuration is competitive for this length on cost alone.

The closest fewer-camera alternative — one 200 m unit plus one 250 m unit — costs approximately RM8,421 and eliminates one installation point. A saving of one pole would need to be valued at over RM3,444 for this to be economical, which is unlikely under standard installation conditions.

**Option B — Better security — 3 × DS-2DE5425 \+ 1 × Dahua SD29404DB-GNY — RM5,691**

Where a specific section of the 450 m road carries higher risk — a poorly lit stretch, an entry point, or a pedestrian crossing — a medium-range supplementary unit can be added at that point without reworking the primary three-camera layout.

![][image12]Total camera cost: **3 × RM1,659 \+ RM714 \= RM5,691**

 

## **4.6 550 m Roads  \[2 streets\]**

### **Option A — Four cameras — Recommended**

**4 × DS-2DE5425 — 150 m IR — RM6,636**

600 m of aggregate rated IR for a 550 m road, providing 50 m of combined margin.

![][image13]

### **Option B — Three cameras, fewer installations**

**2 × DS-2DE7A425IW-AEB(T5) \+ 1 × DS-2DE5425 — RM7,863**

**![][image14]**

Three installation points instead of four. RM1,227 more in camera cost. Total rated reach of 550 m provides no margin for overlap or low-light tolerance.

Four 150 m cameras is the preferred design. The three-camera option is only justified if eliminating one installation point saves more than RM1,227, and only where road lighting is consistently adequate.

 

 

**Design Conclusions**

The pricing structure naturally consolidates the system around a small set of camera roles.

| Camera | Role in design | Rationale |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Hikvision DS-2DE5425IW-AE(T5) — 150 m IR** | Primary | RM138 more than the 100 m unit; 50 m additional IR makes it the default for all new installations. Draws up to 24 W (0.576 kWh/day), 6 W more than the 100 m unit |
| **Hikvision DS-2DE7A425 — 200 m IR** | Installation-point saver | Justified where eliminating one networked pole location saves more than the RM1,227–1,443 camera premium |
| **Dahua SD29404DB-GNY — 50 m IR** | Short section filler | RM714; useful for end segments where a full long-range unit would be disproportionate |
| **Dahua SD6E445MB-HNR-A-PV1 — 250 m IR** | Specialist application | Appropriate where 45× zoom, warm-light deterrence, or very long single-camera reach is specifically required |
| **Hikvision DS-2DE4425 — 100 m IR** | Retained for reference | Not recommended for new deployments; 150 m unit offers materially better performance for RM138 more |

The system standardises around the 150 m Hikvision as the primary unit, the 200 m Hikvision as a strategic alternative where infrastructure cost justifies it, the 50 m Dahua as an economical short-section option, and the 250 m Dahua as a specialist choice outside the standard procurement.
